caps: Why do Hindus | walk around a temple | *CLOCKWISE?*
lines.tts: Why do Hindus walk around a temple clockwise?
It's called pradakshina. Dakshina means right.

caps: You keep God | on your *RIGHT SIDE,* | all the way round.
lines.tts: You keep God on your right side, all the way round.

caps: the path the *SUN* | takes every day.
lines.tts: East, then south, then west: the path the sun takes every day.

caps: But in a *SHIVA* temple, | you *NEVER* | finish the circle.
lines.tts: But in a Shiva temple, you never finish the circle.

caps: The water poured | on the *SHIVA LINGA*
flows out through | a channel to the north: | the *SOMASUTRA.*
lines.tts: The water poured on the Shiva linga flows out through a channel to the north: the Soma sootra.

caps: That water is | *TIRTHA,* holy. | You never | *STEP OVER IT.*
lines.tts: That water is teertha, holy. You never step over it.

caps: You walk round | until you reach it, | then *TURN BACK* | and go the other way.
lines.tts: You walk round until you reach it, then turn back, and go the other way.

caps: The *SHIVA RAHASYA* | says it plainly: | do not cross | the *SOMASUTRA.*
lines.tts: The Shiva Rahasya says it plainly: do not cross the Soma sootra.
Next temple visit, show your child.

caps: Did you know | this *SHIVA* rule? | Comment | *YES OR NO!*
lines.tts: Did you know this Shiva rule? Comment yes, or no!
